ja: 窓のそばに立っている女性が、私の上司の田中さんです。
en: The woman standing by the window is my boss, Ms. Tanaka.
alternatives: The woman who's standing by the window is my boss, Ms. Tanaka.
The woman standing next to the window is my boss, Ms. Tanaka.
point: 「立っている女性」は the woman standing と後ろから説明する

ja: こっちに引っ越してきてからずっと働いている会社は、病院向けのソフトを作っています。
en: The company I've been working at since I moved here makes software for hospitals.
alternatives: The company I've worked at since moving here makes software for hospitals.
Since I moved here, I've been working at a company that makes software for hospitals.
point: 主語は The company で、動詞 makes は長い修飾の後に来る

ja: 福岡で生まれましたが、父が転勤になったので、主にシンガポールで育ちました。
en: I was born in Fukuoka, but I mostly grew up in Singapore because my father was transferred there.
alternatives: I was born in Fukuoka, but because my father was transferred, I mostly grew up in Singapore.
I was born in Fukuoka, but I mostly grew up in Singapore because my dad got transferred there.
point: 「転勤になった」は受け身で was transferred と言う

ja: もし私がもっと英語を話せたら、海外で働いてみたいです。
en: If I could speak English better, I'd like to work abroad.
alternatives: If my English were better, I'd like to work overseas.
If I spoke better English, I'd want to work abroad.
point: 今の事実と違う仮定は could と過去形で表す

ja: 実は、私がこの仕事を選んだ一番の理由は、地元の人たちの役に立てると思ったからなんです。
en: Actually, the main reason I chose this job is that I thought I could help people in my hometown.
alternatives: Actually, what made me choose this job was that I thought I could help the people in my hometown.
Actually, the biggest reason I picked this job is that I thought I could be useful to local people.
point: The reason is that 〜 の形。because でつながない

ja: 差し支えなければ、今のお仕事を始める前は何をされていたのか教えていただけますか？
en: Would you mind telling me what you did before you started your current job?
alternatives: If you don't mind my asking, could you tell me what you did before your current job?
Do you mind if I ask what you were doing before you started your current job?
point: 間接疑問は what you did の語順、did you do にしない

ja: もしあの時友達に誘われていなかったら、私はサーフィンを始めていなかったと思います。
en: If my friend hadn't invited me back then, I don't think I would have started surfing.
alternatives: I don't think I would have started surfing if my friend hadn't invited me back then.
If my friend hadn't invited me back then, I probably wouldn't have gotten into surfing.
If my friend hadn't asked me to join back then, I don't think I'd have taken up surfing.
point: 過去の仮定は if＋had not＋過去分詞、帰結は would have

ja: あなたは仕事で英語を使うことに、もう慣れていますか？
en: Are you used to using English at work yet?
alternatives: Have you gotten used to using English at work yet?
Are you used to using English for work yet?
point: be used to の後は動詞の ing 形

en: There are four people in my family.
alternatives: There are four of us in my family.
My family has four people.
We are a family of four.
point: 「〜人いる」は There are 〜 in my family

ja: はじめまして。私は看護師です。
en: Nice to meet you. I'm a nurse.
alternatives: Nice to meet you. I work as a nurse.
Pleased to meet you. I'm a nurse.
point: 職業には a をつけて a nurse と言う

ja: 差し支えなければ、どういう経緯でこの業界に入ることになったのか聞いてもいいですか？
en: If you don't mind my asking, how did you end up getting into this industry?
alternatives: If you don't mind me asking, how did you get into this industry?
Do you mind if I ask how you ended up in this industry?
point: 「〜することになった」は end up -ing、「業界に入る」は get into
